cards.name: AI_PixelPlay_1
cards.summary: Applies the AI_PixelPlay_1 SVG filter: the object's alpha is blurred (stdDeviation 7), kept inside the shape and added back to the alpha, and the whole filter runs at filterRes 50 x 50, which Illustrator honours. The art renders as a solid black silhouette built from a 50 x 50 grid of blocks laid over the filter region (the object's bounds plus 10% each side): curves and type come out stair-stepped like pixel art, and the silhouette grows by up to one block at every edge. The definition also animates filterRes (1 x 1 up to 200 x 200 and back over 10 s), which only plays in an SVG viewer that runs SMIL and honours filterRes; Illustrator uses the static 50 x 50.
use_for: blocky pixel-art / 8-bit black silhouette of a logo, icon or type that stays live (delete the effect to get the colours back)
retro game-style black knock-out or censor blocks in web SVG graphics
avoid: a clean, smooth black silhouette: the 50 x 50 block grid stair-steps every edge; add a new black Fill in the Appearance panel (Photoshop: Color Overlay) instead
a coloured or partly transparent pixelated result: the filter is fixed black with no settings; for a mosaic that keeps the colours use Photoshop Filter/Pixelate/Mosaic
an even block size: the grid is always 50 x 50 across the object's bounds, so blocks get bigger on bigger art and are non-square on non-square art
relying on the look in a browser: many current SVG viewers ignore filterRes, so the exported SVG shows a smooth black shape

documents that do not carry the default SVG filter set (some opened SVG/PDF files): the filter is missing from Effect > SVG Filters; load it first with Effect > SVG Filters > Import SVG Filter (Adobe SVG Filters.svg in Illustrator's Support Files/Required/Resources/<locale>)

params.name: SVGFilterUIDName
params.does: id of the document SVG filter the live effect points at; for this menu item it is fixed to AI_PixelPlay_1 (a different id gives a different filter)

cards.cost: low: the filter is computed on a 50 x 50 grid, then scaled up

review.changes: summary/use_for/avoid/look rewritten: Illustrator honours filterRes 50 x 50, so the silhouette is a blocky 50 x 50 mosaic (harvest render: piecewise-constant ~7 x 5 px blocks, bbox grown 6 px on each side), not a plain shape; removed the false 'Illustrator renders no pixelation' claim; dropped PS solidFill equivalent (smooth silhouette, not the same result)

verified.note: The whole plate renders as a solid black silhouette built from large square blocks: curves, type and the zigzag are stair-stepped like pixel art and the silhouette grows by about a block at the edges, as the card describes.

cards.name: AI_PixelPlay_2
cards.summary: Applies the AI_PixelPlay_2 SVG filter: a blurred copy of the object's alpha (stdDeviation 7) is used as a bump map, lit by a yellow diffuse light (multiplied into the art) and a strong red specular light (added on top) from the left, all computed at filterRes 50 x 50, which Illustrator honours. The art becomes a 50 x 50 block mosaic over its bounds plus 10%; every fill is pushed to full red with its blue removed, so dark, blue or magenta art goes red and light art goes orange to yellow (the red probe rectangle turned hot red-orange), and the edges darken into stepped rims (on the probe: dark red on the left, dark olive along the top, right and bottom), which swallow a stroke that sits on the edge. In an SVG viewer that plays SMIL the light colours cycle through a rainbow (15 s) and filterRes animates; Illustrator shows one still frame.
use_for: pixelated, hot red-orange 'heat' version of a logo or badge for a retro game / glitch look in web SVG
animated colour-cycling light on a web SVG logo (exported as SVG, viewed in a browser)
avoid: keeping the artwork's own colours: the yellow and red lights recolour every fill and stroke; use Effect/Stylize/Inner Glow or Outer Glow instead
keeping the art sharp: the 50 x 50 block grid pixelates detail and type, with bigger blocks on bigger art

print work: the lit result is rasterized and its look depends on the object size; the filter's distances are fixed user units (points), not a share of the object, so on large artwork the result looks smaller / finer than on an icon
matching the Illustrator look in a browser: many current SVG viewers ignore filterRes, so the exported SVG renders unpixelated

documents that do not carry the default SVG filter set (some opened SVG/PDF files): the filter is missing from Effect > SVG Filters; load it first with Effect > SVG Filters > Import SVG Filter (Adobe SVG Filters.svg in Illustrator's Support Files/Required/Resources/<locale>)

params.name: SVGFilterUIDName
params.does: id of the document SVG filter the live effect points at; for this menu item it is fixed to AI_PixelPlay_2 (a different id gives a different filter)

cards.scripting: app.activeDocument.selection[0].applyEffect('<LiveEffect name="Adobe SVG Filter Effect"><Dict data="U SVGFilterUIDName AI_PixelPlay_2"/></LiveEffect>')
cards.cost: low to medium: blur plus two lighting passes, computed on a 50 x 50 grid

review.changes: summary/use_for/avoid/look: added the 50 x 50 filterRes block mosaic Illustrator renders (harvest render shows stepped 7 x 5 px bands); 'fills turn red-orange' generalised from the red probe to the rule (red forced to full, blue removed, green kept); top rim added; specular is added, not multiplied

verified.note: The art becomes a coarse block mosaic recoloured by the lights: the blue star goes orange-red, the box orange with a bright red left edge and dark red / olive stepped rims, the circle yellow-orange to red, type and zigzag red, the hot-orange pixel emboss the card describes.

cards.name: AI_Shadow_1
cards.summary: Applies the AI_Shadow_1 SVG filter: a small, tight drop shadow. The object's alpha is blurred (stdDeviation 2), offset 4 x 4 units down and to the right as solid black, and the original art is merged on top. Reads as a crisp dark edge on small art; on a full-page group it is only a thin dark line.
use_for: small subtle shadow under web icons, buttons and UI type exported as SVG
a quick live lift for a logo or badge
avoid: a shadow you need to tune (colour, opacity, distance, blur): use Effect/Stylize/Drop Shadow, which has those settings; this filter is fixed black at full strength

large artwork: the filter's distances are fixed user units (points), not a share of the object, so on large artwork the result looks smaller / finer than on an icon; use AI_Shadow_2 or Effect/Stylize/Drop Shadow

documents that do not carry the default SVG filter set (some opened SVG/PDF files): the filter is missing from Effect > SVG Filters; load it first with Effect > SVG Filters > Import SVG Filter (Adobe SVG Filters.svg in Illustrator's Support Files/Required/Resources/<locale>)

cards.name: AI_Static
cards.summary: Applies the AI_Static SVG filter: the art is replaced by very fine fractal noise (baseFrequency 0.5, 10 octaves) cut to the object's silhouette, so it renders as a semi-transparent light grey TV-static grain with faint colour speckle and its own colours disappear. The definition animates the noise frequency (0.5 to 0.7 over 5 s), which plays only in an SVG viewer that runs SMIL, as flickering static.
use_for: TV static / no-signal texture inside a shape or headline for web SVG
animated flickering static in an exported SVG
avoid: adding grain while keeping the artwork's colours: this filter replaces the colours; use Effect/Texture/Grain or Effect/Artistic/Film Grain

print or large art: the grain is fixed in points, so on big artwork it reads as flat light grey; the filter's distances are fixed user units (points), not a share of the object, so on large artwork the result looks smaller / finer than on an icon

documents that do not carry the default SVG filter set (some opened SVG/PDF files): the filter is missing from Effect > SVG Filters; load it first with Effect > SVG Filters > Import SVG Filter (Adobe SVG Filters.svg in Illustrator's Support Files/Required/Resources/<locale>)

cards.name: AI_Woodgrain
cards.summary: Applies the AI_Woodgrain SVG filter. Despite the name it renders no wood stripes: fractal noise (baseFrequency 0.05, 10 octaves) is mapped to an orange-to-dark-brown ramp and cut to the object's shape, so the art becomes an opaque orange mottled cloud texture (fire, cork or sponge-like) and its own colours are lost. The definition also builds a shadow and a lit bevel, but they are not merged into the output, so neither shows.
use_for: warm orange cloud / fire / cork texture inside type or shapes for web SVG
a quick textured fill for a retro badge
avoid: real wood grain: this filter makes mottled clouds, not stripes; try the graphic style 'RGB Wood Grain' (Window > Graphic Style Libraries > Textures) or a wood pattern

keeping the artwork's colours or adding a shadow: neither happens; add Effect/Stylize/Drop Shadow separately; the filter's distances are fixed user units (points), not a share of the object, so on large artwork the result looks smaller / finer than on an icon

documents that do not carry the default SVG filter set (some opened SVG/PDF files): the filter is missing from Effect > SVG Filters; load it first with Effect > SVG Filters > Import SVG Filter (Adobe SVG Filters.svg in Illustrator's Support Files/Required/Resources/<locale>)

cards.name: Apply SVG Filter
cards.summary: Opens the Apply SVG Filter dialog, which lists every SVG filter defined in the document (the default AI_ set plus any imported or new ones) with a preview, and applies the chosen one as a live effect. The dialog can also edit a filter's SVG code, make a new filter or delete one. What the result looks like depends entirely on the filter chosen; the harvest default AI_Alpha_1 masks the art with turbulence, leaving a faded, marbled version of its own colours with clear vein-like gaps.
use_for: applying or swapping any document SVG filter, including custom hand-written ones
editing an SVG filter's feTurbulence / feGaussianBlur / lighting values to tune a look
web graphics exported as SVG where the filter should stay live in the browser
avoid: print work needing exact control: SVG filters rasterize and their distances are fixed in points; prefer the Illustrator / Photoshop Effects with real settings (Effect/Stylize/Drop Shadow, Effect/Texture/Grain)
naming a filter the document does not define: the effect has nothing to render; import it first with Import SVG Filter

params.name: SVGFilterUIDName
params.does: id of the document SVG filter to apply (one of the names listed under Effect > SVG Filters)
params.typical: AI_Alpha_1, AI_Shadow_2, AI_Turbulence_3 or a custom filter id

params.name: DisplayString
params.does: label Illustrator shows for the effect in the Appearance panel
params.typical: SVG Filter:<filter id>, written by Illustrator

cards.scripting: app.activeDocument.selection[0].applyEffect('<LiveEffect name="Adobe SVG Filter Effect"><Dict data="U SVGFilterUIDName AI_Alpha_1"/></LiveEffect>')  // or app.executeMenuCommand("Live SVG Filters") to open the dialog
cards.cost: depends on the filter: blurs and offsets are light, multi-octave turbulence and lighting are heavier

verified.note: With the harvested default filter AI_Alpha_1 the frame equals the AI_Alpha_1 frame: a faded, mottled version of the plate's own colours with clear vein-like gaps, as the card describes.

cards.name: Import SVG Filter
cards.summary: Opens a 'Select an SVG file' dialog and imports the <filter> definitions from that SVG file into the current document, so they appear under Effect > SVG Filters and in the Apply SVG Filter dialog. It changes nothing on the artboard by itself.
use_for: loading custom hand-written SVG filters (grunge, duotone, glow) into a document
restoring the default AI_ filter set into a document that lacks it (import Adobe SVG Filters.svg from Illustrator's Support Files/Required/Resources/<locale>)
avoid: unattended scripts: the command stops at a modal file dialog and takes no path argument
expecting a visible change: apply the imported filter afterwards with Apply SVG Filter or its menu item
cards.scripting: app.executeMenuCommand("SVG Filter Import")  // opens the 'Select an SVG file' dialog; the file must be picked by hand
cards.cost: none on the artwork; adds filter definitions to the document

verified.note: Untested: listed in gallery/ai_effect/not_rendered.json (status needs_input: it stops at a 'Select an SVG file' dialog and takes no path), so there is no frame.

second_opinion.note: Harness check: not_rendered.json lists it by rule; it imports filter definitions and draws nothing by itself, so a frame could only show a filter applied afterwards, and the card makes no frame-based claim.
